issues.failure_explanation: The pointwise inequality is false for every α in [1,2]. For α=1 take f=cos x_1, g=cos x_2: (-Δ)^{1/2}(fg)=√2 cos x_1 cos x_2 while the right side is 2 cos x_1 cos x_2, so the inequality fails wherever cos x_1 cos x_2<0. For α=2 take f≡1, g=cos x_1: at x_1=π the left side is −1 and the right side is C(2)·(−1)=−2. Moreover a one-sided pointwise inequality cannot yield a bound on the absolute value of an inner product, yet (est_nonl) uses it exactly this way. The norm inequality (Kato–Ponce type) is true but not with the stated constant and not by the stated argument; more importantly, the key step in (est_nonl) needs the commutator structure ((−Δ)^{(1+α)/2}(u∂_1u),(−Δ)^{(1+α)/2}u) = ([(−Δ)^{(1+α)/2},u]∂_1u, ·) + (u∂_1 w, w), which is not what the lemma provides.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Lemma 2.2 by the Kato–Ponce commutator estimate ‖[J^s,u]∂_1u‖ ≤ C‖∇u‖_∞‖u‖_s (on the torus) and rewrite (est_nonl) via the commutator splitting plus integration by parts.
issues.overall_effect: The nonlinear estimate (est_nonl), hence (diffine), the bound (bd3), existence/uniqueness and the error estimate that uses (bd3), are unsupported as written.
issues.title: Pointwise fractional product inequality is false; a priori H^{1+α} estimate rests on it
issues.why_classification: The a priori estimate survives, but only via a different, nontrivial (though standard, citable) commutator lemma replacing a false one.

issues.failure_explanation: Bound (bd3) is proved only on [0, T̄] with T̄ = 1/(C‖u_0‖_{1+α}) and gives ‖u_N(T̄)‖_{1+α} ≤ 2‖u_0‖_{1+α}. Restarting from t=T̄ yields an existence time T̄/2, then T̄/4, etc.; the total time 2T̄ is finite. The remark's premise that (bd3) holds uniformly in time is precisely what is to be proved, so the continuation is circular. The paper's conserved quantities (mass, L^2, Hamiltonian) control only H^{α/2}, not H^{1+α}, so no global H^{1+α} bound is available in the source. Consequently the claimed solution on [0,T] for all T ≥ 0 is unsupported.

The only analysis in the source (Lax–Milgram) has continuity constant M∼N^{α+1}, so Céa-type reasoning yields no N-uniform estimate. Writing e_N=Π̃_Nw−Π_Nw, coercivity gives (K−K_0)‖e_N‖² ≤ ‖Π_Nw−w‖·‖(I−Π_N)∂_{x_1}(u e_N)‖, and with u merely C^1 the last factor is only controlled by N‖e_N‖, giving a rate suboptimal by one power of N; the claimed optimal rate under u∈C^1 with r≥0 arbitrary is therefore unsupported. Additionally, the derivation of (proj_erro2) takes r proportional to N inside (proj_erro), which requires the constant C to be uniform in r, a property never stated or proved.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof is the generic RK4 Taylor comparison; the only N-dependent content is the size of the elementary differentials of F(t,V)=e^{-Lt}N(e^{Lt}V), whose t-derivatives carry powers of L with entries −im_1|m|^α of size up to N^{1+α}. The Δt^5 remainder involves ∂_t^4F and d^4F/dt^4, i.e., up to L^4N(U), which is bounded uniformly in N only if u^2 has roughly 4(1+α)+1 derivatives, far more than the assumed r ≥ α+5 when α∈[1,2].
